Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-20 - first-reader response (unverified image reading)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or prior reading was revealed to me. The only provenance-like information I saw is (a) the packet path name "stams3-read" and (b) modern pencil shelfmark labels written on the fragments themselves and visible in the images: "Stams, STA, Frg. 163-1r", "...163-2r", "...163-1v", "...163-2v". I did not use these for anything beyond labelling faces.
- I did not identify, search for, or consult any edition. Beyond the stated rules I ran one shell `ls` on the two packet directories to learn the image filenames (packet.json was not opened).
- All 18 images loaded.

IMAGES
- image-001: overview, recto side: two fragments. Left smaller fragment labelled "163-2r"; right larger fragment labelled "163-1r".
- image-002, -003, -006, -007: tiles of 163-2r.  image-004, -005, -008, -009: tiles of 163-1r.
- image-010: overview, verso side: left smaller fragment "163-2v", right larger "163-1v".
- image-011, -012, -015, -016: tiles of 163-2v.  image-013, -014, -017, -018: tiles of 163-1v.
Tiles overlap; repeated lines are noted as overlaps, not counted twice.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Paper (chain/laid lines visible), two columns per face, written in a German vernacular cursive/bastarda-like hand, brown ink. Ruled frame lines faintly visible.
- No running titles visible. No enlarged initials visible in these crops. Some capitals touched/stroked.
- Latin quotations embedded in the German prose are underlined or boxed (e.g. "Celi enarrant", "Sanctificetur nomen tuum"); some Latin passages are not underlined.
- Top lines on every face are faded/abraded (water/dirt staining at top edge); bottom lines are cut through on all faces, so both fragments are trimmed at foot (and 163-2 also at head).
- 163-2 is a strip (approx. 19 lines per column remain); 163-1 is taller (approx. 21-22 lines per column remain).
- Tentative interpretation: continuous vernacular devotional/catechetical prose with Latin scriptural/patristic citations; 163-1 discusses petitions of a prayer one after another ("Sanctificetur nomen tuum", "Adueniat regnum", "fiat voluntas", "panem nostrum"), and 163-1v discusses sin of pride / detraction and a ladder ("laiter") with seven rungs. 163-2r discusses heathen idol offerings and flies (belzebub); 163-2v discusses offering of turtle doves and Simeon in the temple. I do not infer author or work.
- Marginal: 163-2r top left margin has a small later mark resembling "827" or "Q27" (image-006 line 1 level) and a short faded scribble below it (image-006 line 2 level). A paragraph/dash mark in left margin at image-006 line 12.

SELECTED SPANS: essentially all legible lines of all eight columns were read. Unread/weak: the first 1-3 faded lines at the head of each column, and the cut-off last line of each column.

Conventions: (xx) = expansion of abbreviation; ? after a word = uncertain; [illegible] = not read. ' marks for superscript/abbreviation were expanded where obvious and flagged where not.
